name: B. R. Ambedkar
role: Jurist, social reformer and chair of the Constitution Drafting Committee (1947-1950); Labour Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1942-1946); India's first Law Minister (1947-1951)
summary: Jurist and leader of the movement against untouchability, who argued for the annihilation of caste, a secular constitution with entrenched rights and guaranteed representation for disadvantaged communities, and, in 1947, State socialism written into the constitution under parliamentary democracy. From 1951 he dropped any fixed economic pattern for pragmatic, production-first policies, rejected communist dictatorship and violent revolution, opposed Nehru's non-alignment in favour of the free democracies, and in 1956 converted to Buddhism.

sources.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches, Vol. 1 (Annihilation of Caste; States and Minorities, 1947)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar (ed. Government of Maharashtra)
sources.usedFor: Annihilation of Caste (1936): caste as hierarchy, destroying the authority of the Shastras and Vedas, 'consent of the governed' (electorates passage); States and Minorities (1947) proposal: state ownership of key and basic industries, insurance, state-run agriculture, compensation for acquired land, no right of secession, offence of private discrimination; Thoughts on Linguistic States (1955): one State one language, Hindi as the official language of every State, splitting large linguistic areas; States and Minorities: rights to vote and hold office, right to convert, no State religion, equal access, remedies, minority representation in the executive, settlement rules; Annihilation of Caste: state control of priests, religion of principles, social reform before political reform; 1919 evidence to the Southborough Committee (proportional representation)

sources.title: Buddha or Karl Marx (1956)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Ambedkar's account of the Buddha's creed, his surviving Marxian claims (class conflict, exploitation by private ownership), rejection of the economic interpretation of history as the only explanation, rejection of violence and dictatorship as means, reason and inquiry in religion; spiritual and material values, rejection of 'religion is opium' for Buddhism, Russian dictatorship and backward countries, disarmament

sources.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches, Vol. 13 (Constituent Assembly Debates)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Draft Constitution speeches: Union of India and no right of secession; uniform civil code (Article 35) debate, 1948; 25 November 1949 final speech ('grammar of anarchy', social democracy, hero-worship, constitutional methods); single judiciary; 4 November 1948 speech: President as symbol of the nation bound by ministers' advice, flexible federation, village as 'a sink of localism'; 1949 debate on abolishing the death sentence

sources.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches, Vol. 2 (Bombay Legislature, Simon Commission, Round Table)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: 1938 Bombay Legislative Assembly birth-control resolution (drafted by him, moved by P. J. Roham); critique of the land revenue system as proportionate rather than progressive; 1938 speeches against the Industrial Disputes Bill (right to strike); 1937 speech against the Ministers' Salaries Bill; 1928 Simon Commission report on a second chamber

sources.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches, Vol. 8 (Pakistan or the Partition of India, 1940)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Argument that transfer of populations (Turkey, Greece, Bulgaria) is the only lasting remedy for communal conflict; Muslims' right to self-determination, 'Hindu Raj must be prevented', voluntary rather than compulsory transfer of minorities

sources.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches, Vol. 10 (Labour Member speeches, 1942-1946)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: As Labour Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council: wartime labour measures, compulsory arbitration, limits on strikes; labour's interests; 1942 broadcast 'Why Indian Labour is Determined to Win the War' (nationalism, independence, pacifism); 1943 speech 'Labour and Parliamentary Democracy' (labour party, trade unions, economic interpretation of history)

sources.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches, Vol. 15 (Parliamentary Debates, 1950s)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Parliamentary speeches on abolition of zamindari intermediaries and land to tillers (collective farming remark); estate duty as a tax on capital; 26 August 1954 Council of States speech on foreign policy (communism, co-existence, SEATO, Korea and Indo-China partitions, Tibet)

sources.title: Principles of the Republican Party of India (1956)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar (party programme)
sources.usedFor: Party principles: equality before the law, priority for those who had no opportunity, State obligation to free every Indian from want, parliamentary system as the best form of government

sources.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches, Vol. 14 Part II (Hindu Code Bill debates)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Hindu Code Bill: monogamy to be enforced by law for all sections, women's economic rights, 'Ours is a secular state'; Annexure I, his 10 October 1951 resignation statement (foreign policy, Kashmir partition, East Bengal)

sources.title: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches, Vol. 17 Part III (speeches on parliamentary democracy)
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Speech on the value of a two-party system and a parliamentary opposition in a parliamentary democracy; speech on the need for an opposition in parliamentary democracy; 1938 Manmad speech naming Brahmanism and capitalism as the workers' two enemies

sources.title: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of career: Labour Member, Drafting Committee chair, Law Minister, Mahad satyagraha, 1927 Manusmriti burning, Poona Pact, 1956 conversion, views on communism

sources.title: Ambedkar: Towards an Enlightened India
sources.author: Gail Omvedt (Penguin, 2004)
sources.usedFor: Shift from state socialism (States and Minorities, 1947) to a pragmatic 'no preconceived pattern' economic policy in the 1952 SCF manifesto; move toward a social democratic position; 1956 'Buddha or Karl Marx'; 1928 memorandum rejecting communal electorates even for Muslims

sources.title: Election Manifesto of the Scheduled Castes Federation (1951), in Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches, Vol. 17 Part I
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Principles (every Indian an end in himself, State a means), policy not tied to any ism, birth control, no fixed pattern of industry, large mechanised farms, Big Business and Congress, salt tax, prohibition, foreign policy (Kashmir partition, China, India's first duty to herself, army spending)

sources.title: Bills he introduced in the Bombay Legislative Assembly, 1937 (Khoti Abolition Bill No. XX; Hereditary Offices Act Amendment Bill No. XXIII), in Writings and Speeches, Vol. 2
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Bill to abolish the Khoti landlord system and make the cultivators occupants of their land; bill on hereditary watan offices

sources.title: The Hindu Code Bill as moved by him as Law Minister (1948-1951), in Writings and Speeches, Vol. 14 Part I
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Bill provisions: monogamy, divorce petitions open to either spouse, daughter's share and absolute estate for women, civil registration of marriage

sources.title: Bills he introduced as Labour Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1942-1946), in Writings and Speeches, Vol. 10
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Minimum Wages Bill introduced on 11 April 1946

sources.title: Ambedkar: Towards an Enlightened India (reports of his acts)
sources.author: Gail Omvedt (Penguin, 2004)
sources.usedFor: His founding of the Independent Labour Party (1936); his signing of the Poona Pact (1932), which gave the depressed classes reserved seats

sources.title: What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables (1945), chapter 'Gandhism', in Writings and Speeches, Vol. 9
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Defence of machinery and modern civilization as the source of leisure, rejection of Gandhian 'back to nature' and of a sacrosanct class structure

sources.title: The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution (1923), in Writings and Speeches, Vol. 6
sources.author: B. R. Ambedkar
sources.usedFor: Preface: stabilising the rupee's general purchasing power; preference for an inconvertible rupee with a fixed limit of issue over gold convertibility

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Omvedt says his later view combined competition for growth with State action for social justice, so he took neither a market nor a planned position.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1947 proposal put key and basic industries and insurance under State ownership; the 1952 manifesto dropped a fixed pattern and called for nationalisation only where possible and essential, so the later position is qualified.

unions-good.rationale: As Labour Member he framed labour legislation for workers and called strikes wasteful for labour, while also supporting the unions' goals in the wartime debates.

property-fundamental.rationale: States and Minorities proposed that the State acquire land and industry by compensation fixed in the Constitution, and his 1956 essay says private ownership brings power and sorrow and must be removed.

regulate-corporations.rationale: In 1943 he counted it as progress in parliamentary democracy that the state had recognised it cannot be held at bay by corporations that are anti-social in their purpose.

strong-leader.rationale: Quoting Mill, he warned against trusting a great man with powers that could subvert the country's institutions, a caution that bears on bypassing normal checks.

state-harmful.rationale: States and Minorities proposed extensive State ownership and management, and in 1949 he rejected anarchy and insisted on the State's role in securing justice.

decide-locally.rationale: Presenting the Draft Constitution he said the village republics had been the ruination of India and welcomed that the draft discarded the village and took the individual as its unit.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His 1942 broadcast refused nationalism if it means worship of the ancient past and the discarding of everything not local in origin, and urged readiness to borrow in order to remake the body politic.

nation-first.rationale: His 1951 manifesto said India's first duty should be to herself and called the quixotic policy of saving the world a road to ruin.

revolution-justified.rationale: In 1949 he said that where constitutional methods are open there is no justification for unconstitutional methods and that the bloody methods of revolution must be abandoned.

central-planning.rationale: The 1947 proposal relied on a planned State economy, and Omvedt records that his later policy accepted planning for social justice, though he rejected any fixed pattern.

tax-inheritance.rationale: In a 1950s debate he defended the estate duty as a tax on accumulated capital, with no stated view on how high the rates should be.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The 1947 proposal put basic industry under State direction, and the 1952 manifesto called for nationalisation where it was essential.

widespread-small-property.rationale: In 1947 he called consolidation of holdings and tenancy legislation worse than useless and wanted collective farms on State land, and his 1951 manifesto said cultivation on small holdings must be replaced by large farms.

one-party-rule.rationale: Argued that a two-party system and a parliamentary opposition are necessary, and his party programme rejected single-party government.

democracy-best.rationale: His party principles name the parliamentary system as the best form of government, but he doubted that majorities would keep economic plans in place.

right-to-secede.rationale: Presenting the draft Constitution he said the Federation is indestructible and no State has the right to secede from it; Omvedt notes the 1947 proposal likewise has no right of secession.

political-violence-never.rationale: He held that force can be justified in the cause of justice, but judged communist violence harmful and in 1949 said unconstitutional methods were justified only where constitutional methods were closed.

separate-church-state.rationale: In the Hindu Code debate he said that the Constitution makes India a secular state, so the government cannot make law for a particular community on religious lines.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Annihilation of Caste calls for destroying the authority of the Shastras and Vedas, and he publicly burned the Manusmriti in 1927 as a text justifying caste discrimination.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He accepted that classes have conflicting interests, but rejected the economic interpretation of history as its only explanation and gave moral and religious change a large part, a middle position.

reviewHistory.rationale: Accepted that conflict between classes is real, but rejected the economic interpretation of history as the only explanation and gave moral and religious change a central role.
reviewHistory.author: claude-haiku-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: He accepted that classes have conflicting interests, but rejected the economic interpretation of history as its only explanation and gave moral and religious change a large part, a middle position.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

equal-outcomes.rationale: States and Minorities says the soul of democracy is one man, one value, and that the constitution must shape the economic structure as well as the political one to achieve it.

civilizational-union.rationale: In 1954 he dismissed 'Asia for Asiatics' outside the colonial question, saying Asia is a divided house with no unity among its peoples.

limit-population.rationale: His 1951 Scheduled Castes Federation manifesto called population growth so grave an evil that the party would push birth-control propaganda and clinics and would not hesitate over more drastic methods; in 1938 he had drafted a Bombay birth-control resolution.

reviewHistory.rationale: The 1938 birth-control resolution he drafted urged government to promote birth control to limit family units, a narrower point than population growth as a whole.
reviewHistory.author: claude-haiku-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: His 1951 Scheduled Castes Federation manifesto called population growth so grave an evil that the party would push birth-control propaganda and clinics and would not hesitate over more drastic methods; in 1938 he had drafted a Bombay birth-control resolution.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He wrote that the evils of machinery and modern civilization are due to a social organisation that sanctifies private gain, and that machinery and civilization are indispensable to free man from the life of a brute.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He held that a democratic society's slogan must be machinery and more machinery, civilization and more civilization.

restore-past-order.rationale: He rejected the Brahminical social order and argued that caste's sacredness must be destroyed, and the Buddha essay presents a moral order as the way forward rather than a return to the past.

results-over-ideology.rationale: His 1951 manifesto said the party's policy is tied to no dogma or ism and will adopt any plan of betterment whatever its origin, with an outlook rational and empirical rather than academic.

direct-action.rationale: In his 25 November 1949 speech he said that civil disobedience, non-cooperation and satyagraha should be abandoned where constitutional methods are open.

means-match-ends.rationale: Argued that the means determine the lasting result: moral change by non-violent means serves the end better than force, which he saw as building dictatorship.

return-to-foraging.rationale: He rejected the Gandhian return to nature as a return to nakedness and squalor.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Annihilation of Caste says civilised society needs a division of labour, and objects only to caste's division of labourers into water-tight compartments.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Accepted the surviving Marxian claim that private ownership gives one class power and exploits another, and his 1956 party principles speak of exploitation of class by class.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He rejected the dictatorship of the proletariat as a means, arguing that a dictatorship removes the right to criticise the government, and he defended parliamentary democracy.

collective-farming.rationale: States and Minorities proposed collective farms on State-held land, and in the 1950s parliamentary debate he said he would have liked the State to create collective farming, though he accepted tenure reform.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Argued for group rights for the depressed classes, including minority electorates, on the principle that a minority must have a say in its own representation.

positive-liberty.rationale: States and Minorities argued that the economic power of the more powerful limits the liberty of the less powerful, and that the State must act to secure it.

organic-representation.rationale: He welcomed that the Draft Constitution adopted the individual rather than the village as its unit.

total-state.rationale: His 1951 manifesto made the State only a means to each Indian's development in his own way.

bound-labor.rationale: His 1937 Khoti Abolition Bill would have freed the cultivators under khot landlords by making them occupants of the land they held.

universal-morality.rationale: His account of the Buddha's creed presents a set of moral principles (equality, fellowship, truth, non-violence) as a law of life that rests on reason rather than authority.

economic-freedom.rationale: Nulled: his 1949 warning that political democracy cannot last without social democracy and economic equality at its base is about equality, not about freedom of the economy from the state, so it does not settle this statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: In his 1949 speech he said political democracy cannot last without social democracy and economic equality at its base, a view close to but not the same as the statement.
reviewHistory.author: claude-haiku-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled: his 1949 warning that political democracy cannot last without social democracy and economic equality at its base is about equality, not about freedom of the economy from the state, so it does not settle this statement.

national-self-determination.rationale: His 1942 broadcast praised self-determination as one of the two principles of the French Revolution, and in 1940 he held that the Muslims cannot be deprived of it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Buddha's creed as he gives it requires that nothing be accepted as infallible and that all matters be subject to inquiry, with religion relating to the facts of life.

class-collaboration.rationale: He called Brahmanism and capitalism the two enemies of India's workers, and attacked Gandhism for treating the division of owners and workers as a sacrosanct, permanent part of society.

workers-nation.rationale: He told labour in 1942 that its creed is internationalism and nationalism only a means, and in 1943 warned workers against being led away by appeals to nationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: His 1947 constitutional draft barred disqualifying any citizen from public office, or from any trade or calling, by reason of sex.

reviewHistory.rationale: In the Hindu Code debate he called for monogamy to be enforced for all sections and for women's economic rights to be safeguarded, which runs against separate legal roles.
reviewHistory.author: claude-haiku-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: His 1947 constitutional draft barred disqualifying any citizen from public office, or from any trade or calling, by reason of sex.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

racial-segregation-law.rationale: His 1947 draft guaranteed full and equal enjoyment of schools, inns, wells, roads, conveyances and places of public resort, with limits only if applicable alike to every race, class, caste, colour or creed.

proportional-representation.rationale: In his 1919 evidence to the Southborough Committee he called proportional representation an improper remedy for minorities, since it represents views while electors vote for members of their own group.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: In the Hindu Code debate he said women are not oppressed only in Hindu society, and he pressed for legal reform of women's marriage and property rights.

night-watchman-state.rationale: States and Minorities proposed State ownership of key industries, insurance and land, well beyond defence, justice and property protection.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Annihilation of Caste and his later account of the Buddha's creed both insist that all human beings are equal and that worth, not birth, is the measure of a person; the 1956 party principles require equality before the law.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: In the 1948 Constituent Assembly debate on Article 35 he argued that Parliament should secure one civil code applicable to all citizens irrespective of religion, and defended it against the Muslim-law objections.

restrict-conversion.rationale: His 1947 constitutional draft guaranteed every citizen the free exercise of religion including the right to profess, to preach and to convert.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Argued that government must rest on the consent of the governed, and that a majority community may not claim separate electorates because that would govern the minority without its consent.

population-transfer.rationale: In Pakistan or the Partition of India he proposed a treaty for state-aided migration of minorities between the two states, but called compulsory transfer prima facie wrong and held that it should be left to those who declared they wished to move.

reviewHistory.rationale: In Pakistan or the Partition of India he argued that the transfer of populations is the only lasting remedy for communal peace and cited the exchanges in Turkey, Greece and Bulgaria.
reviewHistory.author: claude-haiku-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: In Pakistan or the Partition of India he proposed a treaty for state-aided migration of minorities between the two states, but called compulsory transfer prima facie wrong and held that it should be left to those who declared they wished to move.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: In Buddha or Karl Marx he wrote that violence cannot be altogether dispensed with and that, where the end justifies it, force is a legitimate means.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: States and Minorities defends State socialism as a way to remove the power of the more powerful to impose arbitrary restraints on the less powerful, which he saw as the real threat to the employee's liberty.

separated-powers.rationale: In the Draft Constitution he argued for a single judiciary separated from the executive, and for the independence of the courts.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The 1956 party principles give priority in opportunity to those who have had none and oblige the State to free every Indian from want; the draft directive principles asked for special care for weaker sections.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: In 1938 he attacked the Bombay Industrial Disputes Bill for penalising strikes and called the right to strike part of the right to freedom, but as wartime Labour Member he defended limits on strikes and compulsory arbitration.

reviewHistory.rationale: As Labour Member he defended wartime limits on strikes and the compulsory arbitration power, saying it gave labour what it had struggled for.
reviewHistory.author: claude-haiku-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: In 1938 he attacked the Bombay Industrial Disputes Bill for penalising strikes and called the right to strike part of the right to freedom, but as wartime Labour Member he defended limits on strikes and compulsory arbitration.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Thoughts on Linguistic States argues that mixed States breed faction fights and discrimination incompatible with democracy, and that one State, one language is the only solvent of racial and cultural conflicts.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: His 1947 draft let the right to apply for a writ such as habeas corpus be suspended in cases of rebellion or invasion when public safety requires it.

party-controls-media.rationale: His 1947 draft barred any law abridging the freedom of speech, of the press, of association and of assembly except for public order and morality.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: In 1937 he protested against the Congress Ministers' Salaries Bill, arguing that ministers' pay must be high enough to attract competent men to the executive.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He explained that under the Draft Constitution the President, unlike the American one, is bound by his ministers' advice and cannot dismiss ministers who command a majority in Parliament.

clerical-rule.rationale: Annihilation of Caste would put Hindu priests under State examination, licence and discipline, and he defended a secular state in the Hindu Code debate.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: As Labour Member he urged Indian labour to back the Allied war effort against Nazism despite the non-co-operation campaign.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: He called the Indian village a sink of localism and a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism that survived only on a low, selfish level.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: In 1954 he condemned cutting up culturally one countries such as Korea and Indo-China, yet his 1951 manifesto wanted India's partition accepted as settled and never reopened.

death-penalty.rationale: In the 1949 Constituent Assembly debate on criminal appeals he said he would much rather support abolition of the death sentence altogether, citing India's belief in non-violence.

religious-exemptions.rationale: His 1947 draft said no person shall be permitted to refuse to fulfil any obligation of citizenship on the ground of caste, creed or religion.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: His 1942 broadcast said external independence is quite compatible with internal slavery and that the worth of independence depends on the kind of government and society that is built.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Buddha or Karl Marx says a Russian dictatorship would be good for all backward countries though not permanently, while States and Minorities rejected dictatorship even as the price of State socialism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Treated private ownership as justified only insofar as it does not bring power to one class and sorrow to another, and called for its removal for the good of society.

collective-defense.rationale: He backed SEATO as an alliance for preventing further communist aggression on the free world.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He listed the states Russia had annexed or subjugated since 1945 as conquests and called Russian liberation liberation followed by servitude.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He proposed that no Hindu could be a priest without passing a State examination and holding a State licence, that priests be under State discipline and that their number be limited by law.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Presenting the draft he described the President as head of the State but not of the executive, who represents the nation but does not rule it and is its symbol.

leader-cult.rationale: In 1949 he warned that hero-worship and devotion in politics is a sure road to degradation and dictatorship, and that gratitude to great men has limits.

land-redistribution.rationale: His 1937 Khoti Abolition Bill would have ended the khots' landlord rights and made the cultivators in possession occupants of their land, with compensation to the khots capped at a small fraction of the assessment.

reviewHistory.rationale: Supported liquidating the zamindari intermediaries and placing the land with those who farm it, while noting that landless labourers would be left out of the change.
reviewHistory.author: claude-haiku-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: His 1937 Khoti Abolition Bill would have ended the khots' landlord rights and made the cultivators in possession occupants of their land, with compensation to the khots capped at a small fraction of the assessment.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

apostasy-punishable.rationale: His 1947 draft protected the right to convert and provided that no person shall incur penalties of any kind by reason of his caste, creed or religion.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: In 1956 he wrote that nobody now accepts the economic interpretation of history as the only explanation and gave moral change a central role, while in 1943 he called the doctrine partly true and said it would hold better if labour put its economic interests first.

reviewHistory.rationale: In Buddha or Karl Marx he says nobody now accepts the economic interpretation of history as the only explanation, and he gives ideas and moral change a central role in social transformation.
reviewHistory.author: claude-haiku-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: In 1956 he wrote that nobody now accepts the economic interpretation of history as the only explanation and gave moral change a central role, while in 1943 he called the doctrine partly true and said it would hold better if labour put its economic interests first.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: States and Minorities wanted economic and individual rights put beyond the reach of a parliamentary majority by the law of the Constitution and enforced by courts with power to issue writs.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: In 1937 he introduced bills to abolish the hereditary Khoti landlord rights and to reform hereditary watan offices.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: His 1947 States and Minorities proposal made discrimination on grounds of race, creed or social status by private employers and commercial concerns an offence.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He argued that rights are real only with remedies, so his draft bars the legislature and executive from overriding the listed fundamental rights and from curtailing the courts' writ powers.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He criticised a foreign policy that made it impossible to obtain financial and technical aid from America for India's industrialisation.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Under his 1947 draft the State would hold the acquired land and let standard farms to village families as tenants, who could be penalised for neglecting the land; he did not restate the plan after 1951.

corporate-influence.rationale: His 1951 manifesto said Big Business finances the Congress and buys power with election funds, and pledged that Big Business would not run the government.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: As Law Minister he moved the Hindu Code Bill, which codified marriage, divorce and the property rights that follow from marriage in law.

religious-nation.rationale: In Pakistan or the Partition of India he wrote that Hindu Raj would be the greatest calamity for the country and must be prevented at any cost.

defeat-communism.rationale: In 1954 he called co-existence between communism and free democracy utterly absurd, likening communism to a forest fire, and said the Western powers ought to have liberated the countries Russia had absorbed.

religion-illusion.rationale: In Buddha or Karl Marx he rejected the communist charge that religion is the opium of the people as inapplicable to Buddhism and argued that only religion could sustain a just society once force is withdrawn.

majority-settlement.rationale: His 1947 draft let a State refuse settlement to persons whose intention is to alter its communal balance.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Buddha or Karl Marx accepts communism's end but rejects its violence and dictatorship, and his 1951 manifesto ties the party to no ism, communism or socialism included, while calling the dislike of capitalism understandable.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He argued that parliamentary democracy needs a two-party system and a working opposition, without which there is no free political life.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He held that government must rest on the consent of the governed, the opposite of authority derived from God.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He told labour in 1942 to reject pacifism as a principle of life and to fight to win the war.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He ended his 1954 foreign policy speech saying it is better for India to align herself with the free nations.

property-franchise.rationale: He wanted adult franchise, and his 1947 draft allowed the right to vote to be withheld only on grounds of immaturity, imprisonment or insanity.

racial-franchise.rationale: His 1947 draft said the right to vote shall not be denied or abridged on any account other than immaturity, imprisonment and insanity, and no office closed for caste or creed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: His 1947 draft made social boycott, including refusing to deal or do business with a person, and promoting such a boycott, criminal offences.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Annihilation of Caste asks that the ancient rules of Hindu life be annulled and replaced by a religion of principles, with one standard book in place of the Vedas and Shastras.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: States and Minorities argued that liberty from State control becomes the dictatorship of the private employer, and that private enterprise would reproduce the inequalities of wealth that should be a warning to Indians.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He faulted the communists for a hatred of religion that would not discriminate between religions, and argued society needs religion.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: His 1947 draft made the executive irremovable for the legislature's term and had each minority's cabinet members elected by that minority's legislators.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He argued that peace bought by surrender to violence is suicide, and that the Buddha allowed force in the cause of justice and safety.

culture-before-state.rationale: Annihilation of Caste argues that political revolutions have always been preceded by social and religious revolutions and calls the thesis that political reform should precede social reform absurd.

second-chamber.rationale: In his 1928 report to the Simon Commission he opposed a second chamber for Bombay, calling the two-chamber system a historical accident with all the faults and none of the virtues.

person-over-state.rationale: The first principles of his 1951 manifesto regard every Indian as an end in himself, with a right to develop in his own way, and the State as only a means to that end.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He wrote that humanity wants spiritual as well as economic values, faulting communism for treating men like pigs to be fattened, and concluded that man must grow materially as well as spiritually.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: He defended a flexible federation in which Parliament can legislate on State subjects in a national interest or emergency and amend most of the Constitution without the States.

communal-electorates.rationale: His 1928 memorandum to the Simon Commission rejected community- and caste-based electorates even for Muslims, though he later demanded separate electorates for the Scheduled Castes.

arms-reduction.rationale: His 1951 manifesto proposed cutting defence spending by Rs. 50 crores a year once Kashmir was settled, and Buddha or Karl Marx says peace would follow if victors disarmed themselves as well as their victims.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: His 1942 broadcast rejected pacifism, saying wars cannot be abolished by refusing to fight when attacked.

workers-own-party.rationale: In 1936 he founded the Independent Labour Party, a party with a working-class identity separate from the Congress.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: His Hindu Code Bill gave the daughter a share in her father's property (half a son's) and turned a woman's limited estate into an absolute estate.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: In his last Constituent Assembly speech he said political democracy cannot last unless social democracy, a life of liberty, equality and fraternity, lies at its base.

women-suffrage.rationale: His 1947 draft barred disqualifying a citizen from public office by reason of sex and allowed the vote to be denied only for immaturity, imprisonment and insanity.

national-church-status.rationale: His 1947 draft said the State shall not recognise any religion as State religion.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: On Kashmir he opposed an overall plebiscite and wanted partition by religion, but accepted a plebiscite confined to the Valley.

simple-living.rationale: He wrote that Gandhism's call of back to nature means back to nakedness, squalor, poverty and ignorance for the mass of the people.

close-ties-china.rationale: He faulted India's championing of Communist China's UN seat for costing American aid, and in 1954 said the Prime Minister had helped China bring its border down to India.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: In his resignation statement he said India should be more concerned with the intolerable condition of 'our people' in East Bengal than with Kashmir.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: His 1951 manifesto proposed re-levying the salt tax, calling its abolition a concession to sentiment that had cost the State revenue without making salt cheaper.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He held that democracy needs organised parties with an opposition facing the government.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: His Hindu Code Bill introduced divorce for Hindus on grounds such as desertion and cruelty, with the petition open to either party to the marriage.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Against Gandhism he argued that only when the machine takes the place of man can toil be lessened and leisure given to every citizen, so a democratic society's slogan must be more and more machinery.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: He granted that convertibility into gold is one way to stabilise the rupee but judged a better way to be an inconvertible rupee with a fixed limit of issue, even proposing to replace silver coins with inconvertible paper.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: His Pakistan plan had both states aid minority members who chose to emigrate, carrying their property and pensions, while ruling out compulsion.

price-stability-first.rationale: In The Problem of the Rupee he held that nothing will stabilise the currency unless its general purchasing power is stabilised, and built his proposals on that aim.

avoid-permanent-military-alliances.rationale: In 1954 he urged the Council of States to weigh SEATO on its merits, as an organisation to prevent aggression on free countries, against the Prime Minister's repugnance to it.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: He proposed reaching State socialism through a constitution under parliamentary democracy, and argued that communism's violent means destroy other values.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: He judged compulsory transfer of minorities prima facie wrong and would leave migration to those who chose it.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: He told an audience that a functional opposition is required, that opposition is the key to a free political life, and that no democracy can do without it.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: In 1942 he said labour cannot allow the living faith of the dead to become the dead faith of the living, nor let the hand of a past with no meaning for the present strangle the spirit of man.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: States and Minorities set out to establish State socialism without abrogating parliamentary democracy and without dictatorship, by writing it into the Constitution.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: His Hindu Code Bill replaced the permitted polygamy of the old law with monogamy and made a marriage to a person with a living spouse void.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: In 1949 he said unconstitutional methods lack justification where constitutional methods are open, leaving them justified where those methods are closed.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: He said the Americans and British should have liberated and freed the nations taken by Russia, and that the free world must be kept free.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: His 1947 constitutional draft made agriculture a State industry, with the State acquiring all agricultural land against debentures; his 1951 manifesto spoke only of co-operative or collective farms and did not repeat State ownership.

reserved-seats-excluded-groups.rationale: He signed the 1932 Poona Pact, which gave the depressed classes reserved seats in the legislatures in place of separate electorates.

civil-marriage.rationale: His Hindu Code Bill provided for marriages to be registered as civil marriages alongside sacramental ones.

notes: Later pass (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-10) bringing the 2026-10-22 Haiku pilot up to rules 5. All twenty volumes of the Writings and Speeches (Dr. Ambedkar Foundation edition, archive.org text) and Omvedt's biography were downloaded to scratchpad/sources/b-r-ambedkar/ and searched theme by theme: economy (States and Minorities 1947, 1951 SCF manifesto, Problem of the Rupee, Gandhism, Labour Member bills), government (Constituent Assembly speeches of 4 Nov 1948 and 25 Nov 1949, Simon Commission report, Bombay Assembly speeches, speech on the opposition), world (1951 resignation statement, 1951 manifesto, 1954 Council of States foreign policy speech, 1942 war broadcast), society and religion (Annihilation of Caste, Buddha or Karl Marx, Hindu Code Bill, Thoughts on Linguistic States, Pakistan or the Partition of India). Record over words: the Khoti Abolition and Hereditary Offices bills (1937), the Minimum Wages Bill (1946), the Hindu Code Bill and the founding of the Independent Labour Party and signing of the Poona Pact answer the statements they settle. Changed answers keep their earlier versions in reviewHistory: land-redistribution now rests on the Khoti bill; population-transfer reversed after reading his rejection of compulsory transfer; restrict-strikes-picketing set to a mixed 0 (1938 defence of the right to strike against wartime limits as Labour Member); economic-freedom and universal-healthcare nulled. Views changed over time: the 1947 State-socialist plan (State ownership of land and key industries) gave way after 1951 to 'no preconceived pattern', so land answers from 1947 alone are low. Caste is not race in his own analysis (Castes in India), so statements about race and racial injustice are left null. No books of his are in the local reference library or Gutenberg selection. Themes searched with little result: immigration, ecology, technology regulation, sexuality and family law beyond the Hindu Code, international institutions and trade.
